newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Higher Canada wheat crop to help replenish stocks.
newsitem.headline: Higher Canada wheat crop to help replenish stocks.

text.p: Canadian wheat exports should not exceed 20 million tonnes this year despite higher production, with instead the extra output going to replenish stocks, a Canadian wheat official said.

"Production has risen but I expect exports to be no higher than 20 million tonnes while carry-out stocks will increase," Richard Klassen, commissioner at the Canadian Wheat Board, told an international wheat conference in Rio de Janeiro.
Stocks at the end of the 1995/96 crop year (August/July) fell to 5.7 million tonnes. However carry-out stocks at the end of 1996/97 could rise to between eight to 10 million tonnes, Klassen said.
"The limitation on our exports will be dictated by our ability to move tonnages logistically," Klassen said.

Canadian wheat production should reach 29 million tonnes this year, up from 25 million in 1995/96 when exports reached only 16 million tonnes, well below the average export program in recent years of 20 million tonnes.

It is by no means guaranteed this year's rise in output will be sustained in 1997/98 given the recent fall in international prices which, if not reversed, may cause some farmers to reconsider their options next year, Klassen said.
"If the price falls too low, I believe our farmers will reassess their situation," he said, adding that canola might be one alternative for disappointed wheat farmers.
Wheat production costs including fertilizers, were in the region to $100 to $110 a tonne in Canada although transport costs represented a further $40 a tonne, he estimated.

One of the reasons for the recent fall in global prices is the large Argentine crop, estimated at between 14 million and 15 million tonnes, which is being offered at levels significantly lower than other origins.
Argentina for example is expected to supply five million and perhaps up to six million tonnes of wheat to its Mercosul partner Brazil which will impact on sales of Canadian wheat to that country.
Last year (1995/96) sales of Canadian wheat to Brazil totalled 1.12 million tonnes but these are expected to fall by 600,000 tonnes in the current crop year.

On other hand, sales of Canadian wheat to Mexico are expected to rise 600,000 tonnes to just over one million tonnes and Venezuela, Peru and Central America are also forecast to be bigger buyers this year of Canadian wheat.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
